*** COFF - THE OFF-TIMER CAPACITOR. DO NOT STRIP THIS NETWORK. *** COFF/ROFF1/ROFF2 implement the SHUNT-DIMMING OFF-TIME COMPENSATION of TPS92515HV datasheet sec 8.3.4 / Figure 14 (TI SLUSBZ6A, extracted this session). WHY IT EXISTS: the OFF-timer normally charges COFF from the OUTPUT voltage, but when the shunt FET shorts the string the output falls below the 1 V VOFT threshold, the timer cannot trip, and every cycle stretches to tOFF(max) = 230 us instead of ~620 ns (Figure 43 shows the failure). Constant inductor ripple and linear shunt-FET dimming are then impossible - and shunt-FET dimming is the ONLY thing that closes PAR-REQ-01's 141 ns wall, so without this network the whole H1 dimming argument stops working. The fix is to charge COFF from VCC (pin 2) in parallel with the output, via ROFF2. VALUE: 470 pF is the datasheet's own preferred value (sec 9.2.1.3: 'Select a COFF between 100 pF and 1 nF. The preferred value is 470 pF'). C0G/NP0 IS MANDATORY, NOT A PREFERENCE - this is a timing capacitor and X7R's voltage coefficient would drift the off-time and therefore the ripple and the dimming linearity. Mount at the COFF pin (pin 1) with a short return to GND.

alternates.note: 8.2 k, JLC Basic, 1274507 in stock - the value TI's literal sec 8.3.4 procedure gives if ROFF2's parallel contribution during NORMAL operation is not compensated. Fitting it yields 545 ns / 79 mA ripple / 795 kHz instead of the architecture's 90 mA / ~700 kHz.

parts.role: *** ROFF1 - OFF-TIME PROGRAMMING RESISTOR, from VLED (the /LEDn_A anode node) to COFF. Part of the sec 8.3.4 / Figure 14 shunt-dimming compensation network - DO NOT STRIP. *** ARITHMETIC: target ripple dIL_pp = 90 mA at L = 47 uH and VLED = 6.8 V gives tOFF = dIL x L / VLED = 622 ns (D = 0.567, f = 697 kHz - this reproduces blocks.md B3 rule 2 exactly). Datasheet eq 7, tOFF = -ROFF x COFF x ln(1 - VOFT/VLED) with VOFT = 1 V and COFF = 470 pF, gives ROFF = 8.32 kOhm -> E24 8.2 k. DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE DATASHEET'S LITERAL TEXT, and it is the reason this is 10 k and not 8.2 k: sec 8.3.4 says 'the value of ROFF1 becomes the previously calculated value of ROFF', but in NORMAL (unshunted) operation ROFF2 sits in PARALLEL with ROFF1 and also charges COFF, from 5 V. The Thevenin of 8.2 k/6.8 V with 47 k/5.0 V is 6.98 kOhm at 6.533 V, which shortens tOFF to 545 ns - ripple 79 mA (-12 %) and f = 795 kHz. Re-solving the Thevenin so the ripple lands back on the architecture's own 90 mA design point: 10 k gives 649 ns, 93.9 mA (+4 %), 668 kHz. 9.53 k (E96) would be the exact solution (622 ns, 90.1 mA) but it is CHECKED AND OUT OF STOCK at LCSC (C23127, 0 pcs), so 10 k is both the practical and the stocked answer. SAME LCSC PART as the R209/R401/R403 10 k entry; split out only so this role note is discoverable per refdes. See OPEN - reverting to TI's literal 8.2 k is a one-line change if P4 disagrees with the re-solve.

*** ROFF2 - THE SHUNT-COMPENSATION RESISTOR, from VCC (pin 2, the internal 5 V regulator) to COFF, in parallel with ROFF1. This is the element that makes shunt-FET dimming linear per sec 8.3.4 / Figure 14 - DO NOT STRIP IT, and do NOT re-source it from +3V3 or any external rail: the datasheet warns of an internal COFF-to-VCC diode that can pull VCC up and start the device with VIN unpowered. Feeding it from the device's OWN VCC pin cannot do that. *** ARITHMETIC: eq 8, tOFF-Shunt = (dIL_pk-pk x L)/(VSHUNT + 0.7). VSHUNT is a DESIGN INPUT the datasheet does not supply - it is the shunt FET's RDS(on) drop at the inductor current. With the selected SSM3K2615R at 0.320 A peak: 0.122 V at its 380 mOhm typ, 0.186 V at its 580 mOhm max. That gives tOFF-Shunt = 5.15 us / 4.78 us, and eq 9, ROFF2 = -tOFF-Shunt/(COFF x ln(1 - 1/VCC)) with COFF = 470 pF and VCC = 5.0 V, gives 49.1 k / 45.5 k -> E24 47 k sits between them. BACK-CHECK AND SENSITIVITY (this is the number to watch): 47 k is exactly right at VSHUNT = 0.158 V, i.e. RDS(on) = 494 mOhm - almost dead centre of the Toshiba's 380-580 mOhm band. Shunted-state ripple error across that band is only -4 % / +3 %. At the pathological limits it is -18 % (VSHUNT = 0, ideal short) and +17 % (VSHUNT = 0.30 V). Those are dimming-LINEARITY errors, not stability errors. VCC's own 4.8-5.2 V regulation band contributes a further +4.7 % / -4.3 %. LOAD: ROFF2 draws 5.0 V / 47 k = 106 uA from VCC, against the datasheet's 500 uA external-load allowance - and each of the four channels has its own VCC pin, so it is 106 uA per device, not 424 uA on one.

DNP. SW-node RC snubber footprint, one per channel. Fitted only if bring-up shows SW ringing (the branch-B VIN abs-max margin is 8 V / 14 % at 57 V). 100 V rated so the same footprint serves branch B unchanged.
DNP. The R of the DNP SW-node RC snubber (10 R + 1 nF). See C303.

alternates.note: Identical silicon in WQFN-16-EP (3x3) - a different footprint, 837 in stock. Leadless, which is acceptable here because the board is PCBA, not hand-built.

SOIC-14, same classic pinout, 29905 in stock - THE STOCK INSURANCE, BUT NOT A FUNCTIONAL DROP-IN: input common mode tops out at V+ minus 1.5 V so the open/short window thresholds must be re-placed, and 800 uA quiescent is 32x the LM339LV. That is a B4 redesign, not a BOM swap.

TI quad open-drain rail-to-rail-input, TSSOP-14, 315 nA/ch - functionally ideal, but stock is 1 pc. Recorded so the search is not repeated. TLV3404, MCP6549 and LMV339 were all swept this session and are all at 0-100 pcs.

parts.role: The firmware-independent over-temperature and NTC-integrity detector (PAR-REQ-12, blocks.md B4). Four channels: emitter hot (90 C, release 75 C) / emitter NTC implausibly cold or OPEN / emitter NTC rail-pinned or SHORT / board hot (110 C, release 95 C). OPEN-DRAIN IS MANDATORY - all four outputs wire-OR onto FAULT, which per ICD s3.3 must NEVER be driven high. RAIL-TO-RAIL INPUT IS EQUALLY MANDATORY, and it is exactly what disqualifies the classic LM339/LM2901: the open/short window thresholds sit at ~3.0 V on a 3.3 V rail, above LM339's V+ minus 1.5 V input common-mode ceiling. LM339LV is the modern 1.65-5.5 V rail-to-rail-input open-drain part on the SAME 14-pin pinout, and its 25 uA TOTAL quiescent current is far inside the '<= 50 uA per channel' requirement (power_tree s4 allows 0.20 mA for the whole device). Hysteresis, never a latch (ICD s8.2, spec-dimming R10).

alternates.note: KUU, 212253 in stock at $0.0275, +-1 % on R25, AND IT HAS A PUBLISHED DATASHEET - but B = 3987 K, not 3950. Effect computed: the emitter-hot tap moves from 89.7 C to 88.9 C, i.e. 0.8 K, so it is an acceptable substitute without re-trimming the ladder.

parts.role: Board over-temperature sensor. Its placement is load-bearing (T-3): ON the copper of the hottest driver stage, but OUTSIDE the ICD s7.6 DC-DC hot zone (2,46)-(36,68). It feeds /ADC1 to the carrier AND the CMP4 board-hot comparator - one sensor, two jobs, which is legal because the comparator input bias is nA-to-pA. THE MODULE'S RT_LED IS THE SAME PART NUMBER BUT IS MODULE BOM, NOT BOARD BOM: it mounts on an RGB package's slug copper (the 1.035 W site, not the white 0.383 W site) and reaches this board through two J5 harness conductors, which is why J5 is 10-way and not 8-way. NOTE: LCSC publishes NO datasheet URL for this part. R25 = 10 k +-1 % and B25/50 = 3950 K +-1 % are its whole specification and both come from the LCSC parametric record; the ladder in R405-R408 is computed from exactly those two numbers. See OPEN.

ADC series-protection resistors on /ADC0 and /ADC1. HELD AT <= 1 kOhm ON PURPOSE: the NTC divider's own Thevenin impedance is up to 5.0 kOhm, so the total source impedance presented to the carrier stays <= 6 kOhm against the ICD s3.3 10 kOhm ceiling (D-T16, L-11). With C401-C403 they form a slow-signal filter, not a pulse filter.

Comparator reference ladder, TOP segment (+3V3 down to the open/cold tap). LADDER ARITHMETIC - ratiometric off +3V3 so every threshold tracks the carrier's ADC reference and is independent of rail accuracy. Total 32.5 k draws 102 uA, matching power_tree s4's 0.10 mA allowance. Taps computed against a 10 k B3950 NTC as the divider's BOTTOM leg, Vnode = 3.3 x Rntc/(10k + Rntc), chain 2.7k / 27k / 1.2k / 1.6k from +3V3 to GND: 3.026 V = -20.7 C (implausibly cold / open), 0.284 V = 89.7 C (emitter hot, target 90 C), 0.163 V = 110.8 C (board hot, target 110 C). THESE FOUR VALUES ARE PROVISIONAL - blocks.md B4 itself calls the thresholds provisional, and they can be re-trimmed at P4 or at bring-up with no footprint change.
Comparator reference ladder, the segment between the emitter-hot tap and the open/cold tap. Full arithmetic on R405.
Comparator reference ladder, the segment between the board-hot tap and the emitter-hot tap. Full arithmetic on R405.

Comparator reference ladder, BOTTOM segment to GND - it sets the 110 C board-hot threshold. Full arithmetic on R405. Extended rather than Basic, but it is a 0603 resistor with 754903 in stock; if a Basic-only BOM is ever required, the Basic 1.5 k moves that threshold to about 113 C.

Positive-feedback hysteresis resistor, one per comparator channel. Sized on the emitter-hot channel: 90 C trip / 75 C release is 0.284 V -> 0.428 V at the divider node, i.e. 146 mV of hysteresis, and against the ~2.6 kOhm ladder source impedance at that tap a 56 k feedback path from a 3.3 V open-drain pull-up gives ~150 mV. HYSTERESIS, NOT A LATCH: ICD s8.2 forbids latching ENABLE locally and spec-dimming R10 forbids cycling in the 0.1-10 Hz band; a >= 15 K band against a heatsinked module's 30-120 s thermal time constant puts any cycle at <= 0.02 Hz, 50x below IEEE 1789's 1-65 Hz seizure band. Provisional together with R405-R408.
